feature: A logo or picture brought into a video
summary: File > Import Media and a drop on the Library now take a PNG, JPEG or HEIC beside your footage. Its tile goes onto the timeline on a track of its own for five seconds, or onto the picture where you let go. An SVG is refused with a short note instead of doing nothing.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording (the tutorial sample works) and have a PNG logo handy. Walk: Scripts/playtest/library-picture-import-walk.json.

try.do: Press Shift Command I and pick a PNG logo.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the logo's tile from the Library onto the recording at two seconds and hold it there.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.
Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command Z, then drag the same tile onto the top right of the picture.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag an SVG from the Finder onto the Library, then over the picture.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Save the video, close it and open it again: the logo tile is still on the shelf.

evaluate: Does a logo landing on its own track over the footage, never covering it, match what you expect from Premiere?
Is five seconds the right length for a still that lands on the timeline?
Is the SVG note enough to tell you what to do, or would you rather the SVG came in soft until it can be kept sharp?
Should a tile let go on the picture run from the playhead to the end (as it does now), or for five seconds like the timeline drop?
rough: An SVG cannot come in yet and the mock's art tiles are SVGs (Sparkle, Star, Cursor, Dot); keeping one sharp at any size is an-svg-logo-comes-into-a-video-and-stays-sharp-a.

The mock lands art on a track called Gfx under the Title track; here it lands on V2 (timeline drop) or on a track named after the layer (picture drop). Covered by a-title-or-a-logo-laid-over-a-video-lands-on-a-t.

The mock captions an art tile as its name over its kind (Sparkle / svg); here it is the file name over its pixel size (Acme Logo.png / 480 x 192), as recording tiles already are. Folded into an-svg-logo-comes-into-a-video-and-stays-sharp-a.
A tile dropped on the picture runs from the playhead to the end of the shot, while one dropped on the timeline runs five seconds; both are the rules those two drops already had.
A Finder PNG let go on the timeline still lands on the picture at the playhead rather than on the track under the pointer; only a Library tile lands on a track.
